figures.alt: Photo of a brown deer in a forest with its ears turned forward and head up, listening and looking.
figures.caption: Sense organs collect information. The brain uses it to decide how to respond.

figures.alt: Photo of one bean seedling in a clear jar of water with the white roots, green stem and leaves all showing.
figures.caption: Roots take in water, the stem carries it, and the leaves catch light. Each part has a job.

figures.alt: Illustration of two students in a classroom. One holds a plain wooden stick up and the other has an open hand ready to catch it as it falls.
figures.caption: The ruler-drop test: the farther the stick falls before it is caught, the slower the response.

figures.alt: Grouped bar graph of how far the ruler fell in cm. Sight: 12, 10, 9. Sound cue: 14, 12, 13. Farther means a slower reaction.
figures.caption: Distance the ruler fell before it was caught. Farther down means slower. Sight: 12, 10, 9 cm. Sound cue: 14, 12, 13 cm.
